authors: Kerkhove, L.-P.; Vanhoucke, M.

authors: Døskeland, Ø.; Gudmestad, O. T.; Moen, P.
title: Use of response forecasting in decision making for weather sensitive offshore construction work
object_and_scale: offshore installation contractor perspective; pipelay case study; operational decision-support service
weather_data_used: operational wave forecasts (2-D spectra + wave-parameter forecasts) for one offshore campaign; forecast RMS error vs wave buoy by lead time
forecast_latency_handled: yes - decision timeline (Fig. 8) states forecast issue time, 8-9 h distribution delay, ~3 h response-calculation processing, and replaces outdated forecasts with the next issue (step 4b)
calibration_target: none statistical; forecast uncertainty handled by lead-time-dependent alpha factors and response limits (no fitted calibrator, no Brier/reliability)
decision_nonanticipatory_yes_no: yes in the case-study decision timeline (only forecasts available before the decision are used); no multi-year chronological-split replay
metrics_used: correctly vs incorrectly identified weather windows; RMS error vs buoy by lead time; qualitative reliability/efficiency
what_it_does_NOT_do_that_this_project_do: multi-year, multi-station, chronologically split replay benchmark; latency rule audited from archive object timestamps (uses stated issue times + assumed processing instead); fitted probabilistic calibration with Brier/reliability diagnostics of the block-exceedance event; cost-loss relative-economic-value curves; exposure-miss accounting across risk settings
threat_level_to_our_novelty: high (already accounts for forecast availability/timeliness, which removes any claim to that concept)

authors: Jafarpour Hamedani, S.; Khedmati, M. R.
title: Optimized planning for weather-sensitive offshore construction operations - An application to float-over installation of super-heavy offshore topsides
object_and_scale: single mega-operation: float-over installation of super-heavy offshore topsides

threat_level_to_our_novelty: high (domain proximity; probabilistic weather windows for one operation)
